nodes.speaker: aria
nodes.text: Hazard cameras spot a boulder field right below us. Autopilot can pick a clear spot, or you can fly it yourself.

variants.text: Long crater shadows hide boulders on the camera feed. Autopilot can pick a clear spot, or you can fly it.
The ridge top is strewn with boulders. Autopilot can pick a clear spot, or you can fly it yourself.

nodes.fact: Landers use lidar, which is laser radar, to map boulders and slopes during descent and steer away from danger.

nodes.speaker: rook
nodes.text: You have the controls! Rookie Kim calls out the altitude: 100 meters... 80...

variants.text: Your hands feel heavy after the rushed launch. Rookie Kim calls: 100 meters... 80...
Rested and steady, you take the stick. Rookie Kim calls: 100 meters... 80...

nodes.fact: Apollo 11's commander Neil Armstrong flew the final minutes by hand to dodge a crater full of boulders.

nodes.speaker: sci
nodes.text: At 20 meters the engine blasts up a blinding cloud of moondust.

variants.text: At 20 meters the engine blasts up a blinding cloud of moondust. We have fuel to hover.
At 20 meters the engine blasts up a blinding cloud of moondust. Hover fuel is getting low.

nodes.fact: Moondust has no wind or water to smooth it, so its grains stay sharp. On Apollo landings it hid the ground at about 30 meters.
